title: Too many men suffering in silence, national health report finds
titleZh: Too many men suffering in silence, national health report finds
author: nosecreek
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Too many Canadian men and boys are facing challenges with their mental health and well-being without the support they need, according to findings from a nationwide consultation that will help shape Canada's first federal strategy dedicated to men's health.

Health Minister Marjorie Michel released the government's What We Heard Report on Nov. 2, highlighting concerns raised by nearly 6,000 Canadians who participated in discussions about the health and well-being of men and boys.
The findings come during Movember, a month dedicated to raising awareness about men's health, and ahead of International Men's Day on Nov. 19.
The report identifies mental health, social isolation and barriers to seeking help as important issues affecting men and boys across the country.
Mental health and social connection among key concerns

comments.author: Dem_Boys
comments.textRawHtml:
Men struggling is no surprise. Today's world is not well suited to their strengths (physical strength, risk taking, aggression, etc..). It's better suited for women and they're winning in a ton of important categories that contribute to quality of life. To compound this, the dating scene for men is abysmal. Women have so much power in the dating market and use it to their benefit as men did before them.

Men especially take this hard. I find men have a very very strong urge to get ahead, succeed, and climb the ladder of success. If they consistently fail at this AND can't find a partner it gets really rough. I have a close friend going through this now and he is contemplating ending it. I'm visiting him everyday just to try to bring a smile to his face

children.author: jimmyjazz14
children.textRawHtml:
You are a good friend and truly the solution to the problem is simply people looking for the people in their lives that are struggling and being there for them, its amazing what just a little acknowledgment from a friend (or even a stranger) can do for someone.

One day I was at a store checking out and the attendant was rather brusk and didn't seem particularly friendly, but he was wearing a watch that I liked and I simply stated that I liked his watch and he lit up, the whole dynamic changed in an instant. I wasn't trying to be nice I literally just liked his watch but after seeing how he opened up and changed after that statement I realized just how much joy can be created with a simple compliment. I try to genuinely compliment people more often now.

children.author: mancerayder
children.textRawHtml:
The dating scene is horrific because dating apps made that imbalance between men and women optionality worse. Women gravitate towards the top 5 or 10 percent of profiles by attractiveness, and feel disappointed they can't find men who want to commit. Men not in that category get almost no hits or when they do, the women are quick to ghost.

As with everything else - information, inequality, wealth creation, manufacturing, even base human desires - technology is a big accelerant to what already exists.

The problem is that the Match Group which owns all the dating sites has no financial interest in your friend finding a partner. Quite the opposite actually.

children.author: port11
children.textRawHtml:
We can flip this on its head.

I’ve grown up mostly friends with queer people and women, given they feel emotionally safer and are just generally more pleasant to be with. Men have it hard, but I don’t think any harder than any other group of people out there.

Now, I’m a dude. I got into clinical depression, trauma therapy, attempt at suicide, you know, the works. I’m very empathetic towards the suffering of other people.

But… men’s struggles can be 80% alleviated by men showing empathy, doing some therapy, and trying to connect with other people. There. Our ‘strengths’ aren’t that useful in the modern world, but failing to adapt and seeking behaviours that would help us thrive is contrary to evolution.

Things have been tipped in favour of women for a bit, which is a correction on the previous environment. And, eventually, it will all harmonise.

I’ve now had 3 separate moments where dudes were making fun of my toddler. You know, the casual snickering, the little comments. Uh, look, it’s a child doing child things. Womp womp, can’t be vulnerable, gotta tear everything down to make ourselves feel good.

I’ve women in my life that date or go on dates with the complete men-children that are perpetually in arrested development, inconsiderate, unkind. They’re not meanies or thugs, they’re just dudes that never learned compassion or empathy, that never had the curiosity of wondering “is the world unfair or am I not adapting to it?”

Men deserve help. We all do. But the Male Loneliness Epidemic is, if not self-inflicted, self-perpetuated. We need, as men, to take responsibility for ourselves and find ways out of this.

comments.author: legitster
comments.textRawHtml:
I read through the underlying report, but the survey itself is extremely unremarkable.

There were only 12 very vague questions - and none actually asked the respondent about how they felt personally: "Where do you believe stereotypes about masculinity primarily come from?"

Only about 2/3 of the respondents even identified as male - this isn't a serious study of how men themselves feel. It's more of a survey about the public perception of men.
